newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Noroeste silent on sale report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Noroeste silent on sale report.

text.p: Brazilian private bank Banco Noroeste said it had no comment on a newspaper report that it had agreed to sell a controlling stake to Spanish banking group Banco Santander SA.

"There is no relevant information to be released to the market and nothing to be added to recent comments by Banco Noroeste regarding that matter," said Jayme Marques de Souza, the bank's Investor Relations director, in a statement sent to the Sao Paulo Stock Exchange (Bovespa).

Banco Noroeste has been plagued by rumors that it will be sold to Banco Santander. At a news conference Thursday on the bank's strategy in Brazil, the president of the Spanish group in Brazil, Antonio Horta Osorio, refused to deny or confirm the rumors.

The statement was sent following a request from Bovespa, which asked Noroeste to clarify the Folha de Sao Paulo daily report today that a preliminary contract of purchase had already been signed by Santander and Noroeste.
The newspaper also said the purchase of Banco Noroeste had already been approved by Brazil's Central Bank, and that an announcement on the deal would be made on July 30.

Banco Santander, which in late March acquired a 51 percent controlling stake in local bank Banco Geral do Comercio, said it is willing to study several ways to expand business in Brazil, which may include buying other banks or building its own branches.
It also said it will study privatization opportunities in the Brazilian banking sector, such as federal bank Banco Meridional and Sao Paulo state bank Banespa.
Banco Noroeste, owned by the Cochrane family, is medium-sized bank, with 90 branches.
